title: Causal Discovery
text: Suppose DAG: define layout use plotting graphs article:  can create data linear Gaussian model corresponding DAG using generate_dag_data(). generate 10,000 samples fixed random seed DAG , let edge coefficients sampled absolute values 0.1 0.9 assigned random signs, standard deviation additive Gaussian noise node sampled log-uniform distribution 0.3 2. R code used generate data stored attribute data frame: goal now recover causal structure data alone. use PC algorithm learn causal structure. One key assumptions causal sufficiency, meaning unobserved confounders. can use PC algorithm “tetrad”, “pcalg”, “bnlearn” engines learn structure data. motivation multiple engines may implement different algorithms, tests, scoring methods, algorithm may implemented differently across engines. , set PC algorithm using Fisher’s Z test, significance level 0.05, pcalg engine. , first define PC method using pc() function, pass disco() function along data. can visualize results using plot() function, explicitly provide layout defined graphs easier compare.  PC algorithm recovers correct causal structure Markov equivalence, represented CPDAG. CPDAG represents equivalence class DAGs encode conditional independencies. first notable feature plot edges directed, others undirected. example, edge X1 Y directed, indicating causal effect X1 Y, reverse direction. contrast, edge X2 X3 undirected, indicating data alone provide sufficient information determine causal direction. orientations X2 %-->% X3 X3 %-->% X2 compatible observed conditional independencies. demonstrate non-identifiability causal direction X2 X3 reversing direction edge data-generating process applying PC algorithm resulting data set.  learn causal structure , demonstrating direction influence X2 X3 determined data alone.
code: cg <- caugi::caugi(   Z %-->% X1,   X3 %-->% X2,   X1 %-->% Y,   X2 %-->% Y ) layout <- caugi::caugi_layout_sugiyama(cg) plot(cg, layout = layout, main = "True DAG") data_linear <- generate_dag_data(   cg,   n = 10000,   seed = 1405,   coef_range = c(0.1, 0.9),   error_sd = c(0.3, 2) ) #> Warning: `generate_dag_data()` was deprecated in causalDisco 1.2.0. #> ℹ Please use `sim_data()` instead. head(data_linear) #> # A tibble: 6 × 5 #>        Z      X3     X1      X2       Y #>    <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> #> 1  0.632  0.297   0.773 -0.256  -0.730  #> 2 -1.67  -1.10   -1.20   1.10   -0.722  #> 3 -0.214  0.713   1.09   0.0264  0.261  #> 4 -1.61  -0.171  -1.21  -0.0346  0.0746 #> 5  1.57   0.0517  0.402 -0.874   1.40   #> 6 -1.08   0.178  -1.09   0.189   0.0591 attr(data_linear, "generating_model") #> $dgp #> $dgp$X3 #> rnorm(n, sd = 0.95) #>  #> $dgp$X2 #> X3 * 0.159 + rnorm(n, sd = 0.507) #>  #> $dgp$Z #> rnorm(n, sd = 1.794) #>  #> $dgp$X1 #> Z * 0.3 + rnorm(n, sd = 1.634) #>  #> $dgp$Y #> X1 * 0.61 + X2 * 0.31 + rnorm(n, sd = 1.216) pc_pcalg <- pc(engine = "pcalg", test = "fisher_z", alpha = 0.05) pc_result_pcalg <- disco(data = data_linear, method = pc_pcalg) plot(pc_result_pcalg, layout = layout, main = "PC (pcalg)") cg_reverse <- caugi::caugi(   Z %-->% X1,   X2 %-->% X3,   X1 %-->% Y,   X2 %-->% Y )  data_linear_reverse <- generate_dag_data(   cg_reverse,   n = 10000,   seed = 1405,   coef_range = c(0.1, 0.9),   error_sd = c(0.3, 2) )  pc_result_reverse <- disco(data = data_linear_reverse, method = pc_pcalg) plot(pc_result_reverse, layout = layout, main = "PC (pcalg) reversed")

title: Causal Discovery
text: practice, unobserved confounding may present, violating one assumptions PC algorithm. Suppose following DAG unobserved confounder U X1 X2: can visualize DAG, marking unobserved variable U red using dashed edges indicate unobserved:  can generate data DAG using generate_dag_data(), afterwards remove unobserved variable U data frame: can apply PC algorithm :  see PC algorithm recover correct causal structure due presence unobserved confounder. particular, found incorrect edge X1 X2.
code: cg_unobserved <- caugi::caugi(   Z %-->% X1,   X3 %-->% X2,   X1 %-->% Y,   X2 %-->% Y,   U %-->% X1 + X2 ) plot(   cg_unobserved,   edge_style = list(     by_edge = list(       U = list(col = "red", fill = "red", lty = "dashed")     )   ),   node_style = list(     by_node = list(       U = list(col = "red", fill = "red")     )   ),   main = "True DAG" ) data_unobserved <- generate_dag_data(   cg_unobserved,   n = 10000,   seed = 1405,   coef_range = c(0.1, 0.9),   error_sd = c(0.3, 2) ) data_unobserved <- data_unobserved[, names(data_unobserved) != "U"] head(data_unobserved) #> # A tibble: 6 × 5 #>         Z      X3     X1     X2       Y #>     <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl> #> 1  0.608   1.42   -1.31  -1.69   1.99   #> 2 -0.716  -0.357  -0.490 -0.561  0.955  #> 3  1.22    1.49   -0.124 -1.48   1.52   #> 4 -0.752  -0.188   0.877  1.35  -1.39   #> 5 -0.0863  0.0156  1.54  -0.926 -0.0833 #> 6 -0.799  -0.929   0.802  0.253 -0.939 pc_pcalg_unobserved <- pc(engine = "pcalg", test = "fisher_z", alpha = 0.05) pc_result_unobserved <- disco(   data = data_unobserved,   method = pc_pcalg_unobserved ) #> The learned graph is not a valid CPDAG because of conflicting edge orientations, which can happen due to statistical errors in finite samples, violations of faithfulness, or latent confounding; it is reported as PDAG instead. plot(pc_result_unobserved, layout = layout, main = "PC (pcalg)")

code: data(num_data) head(num_data) #>         X1        X2       X3         Z        Y #> 1 3.900715  7.048325 6.964806 10.272479 15.35505 #> 2 4.736112  6.236746 5.666022 10.357262 23.36749 #> 3 4.657992 12.169805 9.127046  9.138338 25.32495 #> 4 5.176469  6.392344 6.101088 10.808335 26.75643 #> 5 4.535538 10.305236 7.465185 10.612735 22.67612 #> 6 4.885914 10.018856 7.413312  9.375931 28.03132 plot_layout <- data.frame(   name = c("Z", "X3", "X1", "X2", "Y"),   x = c(0.00, 0.50, 0.00, 0.50, 0.25),   y = c(0.0, 0.0, 0.5, 0.5, 1.0) ) pc_bnlearn <- pc(   engine = "bnlearn", # Use the Tetrad implementation     score = "ebic" # Use the EBIC score   )   ges_result_tetrad <- disco(data = num_data, method = ges_tetrad)   plot(ges_result_tetrad, layout = plot_layout, main = "GES EBIC (Tetrad)") } plot(   pc_result_bnlearn,   layout = plot_layout,   main = "Customized plot",   node_style = list(     fill = "lightblue", # Fill color     col = "darkblue", # Border color     lwd = 2, # Border width     padding = 4, # Text padding (mm)     size = 1.2 # Size multiplier   ) ) print(pc_result_bnlearn) #> <Disco CPDAG: 5 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: X1, X2, X3, Z, Y #>   edges: X1-->Y, X1---Z, X2---X3, X2-->Y, X3-->Y, Z-->Y

title: causalDisco
text: section use dataset tpc_example, contains variables, measured three different life stages: childhood, youth, old age. Since know temporal ordering variables, can incorporate background knowledge causal discovery algorithm. Specifically, know variables measured childhood caused variables measured youth old age, variables measured youth caused variables measured old age. Knowledge encoded creating Knowledge object via knowledge() function. first argument (optional, recommended name matching) specifies dataset. Tiered knowledge can defined using tier() function. , illustrate creating tiered knowledge structure based life stages: details define knowledge, see knowledge article. can view Knowledge object using print(), summary() plot():  plot displays vertical tiers, enclosed shaded rectangle labeled corresponding tier name top. can incorporate knowledge algorithm like . , need pass Knowledge object argument disco() function. use Temporal Peter-Clark (tpc) algorithm causalDisco regression-based information loss test: Similarly, can view results using print(), summary() plot():  Like , tiered knowledge reflected plot layout, variables grouped life stage. Additionally, can customize plot appearance passing additional arguments plot().
code: data(tpc_example) head(tpc_example) #>   child_x2   child_x1    youth_x4 youth_x3  oldage_x6  oldage_x5 #> 1        0 -0.7104066 -0.07355602        1  6.4984994  3.0740123 #> 2        0  0.2568837 -1.16865142        1  0.3254685  1.9726530 #> 3        0 -0.2466919 -0.63474826        1  4.1298927  1.9666697 #> 4        1  1.6524574  0.97115845        0 -7.9064009 -4.5160676 #> 5        0 -0.9516186  0.67069597        0  1.7089134  0.7903853 #> 6        1  1.9549723 -0.65054654        0 -6.9758928 -3.2107342 kn <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   tier(     child ~ c("child_x1", "child_x2"),     youth ~ starts_with("youth"), # tidyselect helper; equivalent to c("youth_x3", "youth_x4")     oldage ~ starts_with("oldage")   ) ) print(kn) #> <Knowledge: 3 tiers | 6 vars> #>   tier(child): child_x1, child_x2 #>   tier(youth): youth_x3, youth_x4 #>   tier(oldage): oldage_x5, oldage_x6 summary(kn) #>        Length Class  Mode    #> vars   2      tbl_df list    #> tiers  1      tbl_df list    #> edges  5      tbl_df list    #> frozen 1      -none- logical plot(kn, main = "Temporal Knowledge") tpc_method <- tpc(   engine = "causalDisco", # Use the causalDisco implementation   test = "reg" # Use the regression-based information loss test ) tpc_result <- disco(data = tpc_example, method = tpc_method, knowledge = kn) print(tpc_result) #> <Disco MPDAG: 6 nodes | 6 edges | Knowledge: 3 tiers> #> Learned graph: #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x1---child_x2, child_x2-->oldage_x5, child_x2-->youth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3-->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6 #> Knowledge: #>   tier(child): child_x1, child_x2 #>   tier(youth): youth_x3, youth_x4 #>   tier(oldage): oldage_x5, oldage_x6 summary(tpc_result) #> Warning: `summary()` was deprecated in causalDisco 1.2.0. #> ℹ Please use `print()` instead. #> <Disco MPDAG: 6 nodes | 6 edges | Knowledge: 3 tiers> #> Learned graph: #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x1---child_x2, child_x2-->oldage_x5, child_x2-->youth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3-->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6 #> Knowledge: #>   tier(child): child_x1, child_x2 #>   tier(youth): youth_x3, youth_x4 #>   tier(oldage): oldage_x5, oldage_x6 plot(tpc_result, main = "TPC reg_test with Temporal Knowledge (causalDisco)")

title: Custom CI tests for causal discovery algorithms
text: interface custom tests depends slightly engine used. causalDisco pcalg use exact interface, bnlearn slightly different now. plan unify interface across engines future release. custom test takes signature function(x, y, conditioning_set, suff_stat, args), (args optional). x y variables tested independence, conditioning_set conditioning set, suff_stat list sufficient statistics needed test (e.g. correlation matrix sample size). function return p-value indicating whether x y conditionally independent given conditioning_set. course suff_stat argument just raw data, efficiency reasons, often better precompute sufficient statistics. example custom CI test partial correlation test based Fisher Z-transform, can implemented follows: can used causalDisco engine follows:  pcalg engine follows:  custom test requires additional arguments, function signature include args parameter, .e. function(x, y, conditioning_set, suff_stat, args), additional arguments can passed list args parameter defining method. bnlearn signature , must pass suff_stat/data directly function, since bnlearn way precompute sufficient statistics pass test function. defining custom test bnlearn, can use either conditioning_set suff_stat z data, argument names bnlearn expects. test function return either: single numeric value (p-value), numeric vector length 2, second element p-value. bnlearn requires first element (test statistic), used. return p-value, dummy statistic automatically injected.
code: my_test <- function(x, y, conditioning_set, suff_stat) {   C <- suff_stat$C   n <- suff_stat$n    vars <- c(x, y, conditioning_set)   C_sub <- C[vars, vars, drop = FALSE]   K <- solve(C_sub)   r <- -K[1, 2] / sqrt(K[1, 1] * K[2, 2])   z <- 0.5 * log((1 + r) / (1 - r))    stat <- sqrt(n - length(conditioning_set) - 3) * abs(z)    pval <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(stat))    pval }  my_suff_stat <- function(data) {   list(     C = cor(data),     n = nrow(data)   ) } data(num_data)  my_tpc <- tpc(   engine = "causalDisco",   test = my_test,   alpha = 0.05,   suff_stat_fun = my_suff_stat ) result <- disco(data = num_data, method = my_tpc) plot(result) my_pc <- pc(   engine = "pcalg",   test = my_test,   alpha = 0.05,   suff_stat_fun = my_suff_stat ) result <- disco(data = num_data, method = my_pc) plot(result) my_test_bnlearn <- function(x, y, conditioning_set, suff_stat, args = list()) {   not_used <- args$not_used   C <- cor(suff_stat)   n <- nrow(suff_stat)    vars <- c(x, y, conditioning_set)   C_sub <- C[vars, vars, drop = FALSE]   K <- solve(C_sub)   r <- -K[1, 2] / sqrt(K[1, 1] * K[2, 2])   z <- 0.5 * log((1 + r) / (1 - r))    stat <- sqrt(n - length(conditioning_set) - 3) * abs(z)    pval <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(stat))    pval }  my_pc <- pc(   engine = "bnlearn",   test = my_test_bnlearn,   alpha = 0.05,   args = list(not_used = "Example of passing additional arguments") ) result <- disco(data = num_data, method = my_pc) plot(result)

title: Incorporating Knowledge
text: Tiered knowledge provides higher-level abstraction expressing systematic ordering assumptions, temporal logical precedence. Internally, tiered knowledge translated collection forbidden edges, exposed separately provides concise structured way express common ordering assumptions. example, consider dataset three groups variables: child, youth, old. may wish enforce child variables precede youth variables, turn precede old variables. can expressed using tiered knowledge. Tiered knowledge enforces edges may point earlier tiers later tiers. Edges within tier unrestricted unless additional knowledge supplied. Suppose observe variables time: first ’s, B’s, finally C’s. ordering implies causal direction go backward time (e.g., B’s cause ’s). tiered Knowledge object captures temporal structure specifying tiers associated variables. numeric tiers used, lower numbers indicate earlier tiers; otherwise, tiers ordered appearance. following specifications encode tier structure: can visualize tiers:  plot shows tiers layers, earliest tiers left latest right. can convert meaning tiered knowledge explicit forbidden edges using convert_tiers_to_forbidden():  Tidyselect helpers starts_with can also used define tiers concise way, just required forbidden edges. Different tidyselect helpers can freely combined within tier definition using +. example, following tiered Knowledge object defines two tiers, “young” “old”, combining tidyselect helpers variables tpc_example dataset:
code: kn <- knowledge(   tier(     1 ~ c(A1, A2),     2 ~ c(B1, B2),     3 ~ c(C1, C2)   ) )  # Same object, since tiers are ordered numerically kn_same <- knowledge(   tier(     1 ~ c(A1, A2),     3 ~ c(C1, C2),     2 ~ c(B1, B2)   ) )  # Functionally equivalent, though not identical kn_almost <- knowledge(   tier(     10 ~ c(A1, A2),     30 ~ c(C1, C2),     20 ~ c(B1, B2)   ) )  # Again functionally equivalent kn_also_almost <- knowledge(   tier(     A ~ c(A1, A2),     B ~ c(B1, B2),     C ~ c(C1, C2)   ) )  # Has a letter, so tiers are ordered by appearance, thus functionally equivalent kn_mixed <- knowledge(   tier(     3 ~ c(A1, A2),     B ~ c(B1, B2),     1 ~ c(C1, C2)   ) ) plot(kn) kn_converted <- convert_tiers_to_forbidden(kn) print(kn_converted) #> <Knowledge: 6 vars | 12 forbidden> #>   vars: A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2 #>   forbidden: #>     B1!-->A1 + A2 #>     B2!-->A1 + A2 #>     C1!-->A1 + A2 + B1 + B2 #>     C2!-->A1 + A2 + B1 + B2 plot(kn_converted) kn_tier_tidyselect <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   tier(     young ~ starts_with("child") + ends_with(c("3", "4")),     old ~ starts_with("old")   ) ) plot(kn_tier_tidyselect)

title: Extending causalDisco with new algorithms
text: Suppose want add Hybrid Parents Children (HPC) algorithm bnlearn. can integrate causalDisco creating new function hpc(). HPC constraint-based algorithm, requires conditional independence test significance level alpha. returns PDAG, set graph_class attribute "PDAG". function takes engine argument, specifies implementation algorithm use. Even though add HPC bnlearn example, set structure allow multiple engines future. ... argument allows us pass additional arguments underlying algorithm test. code hpc() function follows: see hpc() function simple, logic handled make_method() make_runner() functions. defined, HPC algorithm can used like method causalDisco. first construct method using hpc(), pass disco(). demonstrate using included tpc_example dataset:  implement score-based algorithm instead, structure remain . main difference method accept score argument rather test alpha. hybrid algorithm accept test, alpha, score arguments. implement algorithm pcalg rather bnlearn, follow structure change instances "bnlearn" "pcalg".
code: hpc <- function(   engine = c("bnlearn"),   test,   alpha = 0.05,   ... ) {   engine <- match.arg(engine)    make_method(     method_name = "hpc",     engine = engine,     engine_fns = list(       bnlearn = function(...) make_runner(engine = "bnlearn", alg = "hpc", ...)     ),     test = test,     alpha = alpha,     graph_class = "PDAG",     ...   ) } data(tpc_example) hpc_bnlearn <- hpc(engine = "bnlearn", test = "fisher_z", alpha = 0.05) hpc_bnlearn_result <- disco(tpc_example, hpc_bnlearn) #> The learned graph is not a valid CPDAG because of conflicting edge orientations, which can happen due to statistical errors in finite samples, violations of faithfulness, or latent confounding; it is reported as PDAG instead. plot(hpc_bnlearn_result)

what: A fully custom algorithm implemented in R
title: Extending causalDisco with new algorithms
text: show use plain R function wrote algorithm, instead package. causalDisco engine’s CausalDiscoSearch$set_alg() accepts function directly, can reuse data/knowledge/test handling swapping search procedure. constraint-based custom algorithm signature function(data, knowledge, suff_stat), mirroring tpc_run()/tfci_run(). score-based custom algorithm instead signature function(score), mirroring tges_run(); pass type = "score" set_alg() . implement (trivial) constraint-based algorithm just calls tpc_run() whatever test search object configured . wire disco(), knowledge injection return type built-algorithms, wrap CausalDiscoSearch object make_method(), exactly hpc() . One thing watch : search$set_test() doesn’t just resolve test function (afterwards available search$test), also computes sufficient statistic run_search() passes algorithm’s suff_stat argument. my_alg() can now used exactly like built-method:
code: my_alg <- function(test = "fisher_z", alpha = 0.05, ...) {   make_method(     method_name = "my_alg",     engine = "causalDisco",     engine_fns = list(       causalDisco = function(test, alpha, ...) {         search <- CausalDiscoSearch$new()         search$set_test(test, alpha)          my_search_alg <- function(data, knowledge, suff_stat) {           tpc_run(             data = data,             knowledge = knowledge,             suff_stat = suff_stat,             test = search$test           )         }         search$set_alg(my_search_alg)          list(           set_knowledge = function(knowledge) search$set_knowledge(knowledge),           run = function(data) search$run_search(data)         )       }     ),     test = test,     alpha = alpha,     graph_class = "PDAG",     ...   ) } data(tpc_example) kn <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   tier(     child ~ tidyselect::starts_with("child"),     youth ~ tidyselect::starts_with("youth"),     oldage ~ tidyselect::starts_with("oldage")   ) ) result <- disco(   data = tpc_example,   method = my_alg(test = "fisher_z"),   knowledge = kn ) plot(result)

Instantiate correct Tetrad algorithm class. fully qualified class name can identified inspecting Tetrad source code : https://github.com/cmu-phil/tetrad sure browse version corresponding installed Tetrad release. relevant Java classes located : https://github.com/cmu-phil/tetrad/tree/development/tetrad-lib/src/main/java can view custom registered Tetrad algorithms using list_registered_tetrad_algorithms(), reset using reset_tetrad_alg_registry(). structure method function Tetrad algorithm exact bnlearn pcalg, seen . BOSS score-based algorithm, accepts score argument. algorithm returns PDAG, set graph_class attribute "PDAG". can now run my_boss_variant() like method causalDisco.  , using hybrid constraint-based algorithm rather score-based one, structure remain method accept different arguments (e.g., test alpha constraint-based algorithm). Finally, clean custom registered Tetrad algorithm
code: register_tetrad_algorithm(   "my_boss_variant",   function(     self,     num_starts = 1,     use_bes = TRUE,     use_data_order = TRUE,     output_cpdag = TRUE   ) {     self$set_params(       USE_BES = use_bes,       NUM_STARTS = num_starts,       USE_DATA_ORDER = use_data_order,       OUTPUT_CPDAG = output_cpdag     )      self$alg <- rJava::.jnew(       "edu/cmu/tetrad/algcomparison/algorithm/oracle/cpdag/Boss",       self$score     )     self$alg$setKnowledge(self$knowledge)   } ) my_boss_variant <- function(   engine = "tetrad",   score,   ... ) {   engine <- match.arg(engine)    make_method(     method_name = "my_boss_variant",     engine = engine,     engine_fns = list(       tetrad = function(...) {         make_runner(engine = "tetrad", alg = "my_boss_variant", ...)       }     ),     score = score,     graph_class = "PDAG",     ...   ) } # Ensure Tetrad is installed and Java is working before running the algorithm if (verify_tetrad()$installed && verify_tetrad()$java_ok) {   my_boss_variant_tetrad <- my_boss_variant(     engine = "tetrad",     score = "sem_bic"   )   my_boss_variant_tetrad_result <- disco(tpc_example, my_boss_variant_tetrad)   plot(my_boss_variant_tetrad_result) } reset_tetrad_alg_registry()

code: always_empty_runner <- function(alg, ...) {   kn <- knowledge()   list(     set_knowledge = function(knowledge) kn <<- knowledge,     run = function(data) {       cg <- caugi::caugi(         from = character(0),         edge = character(0),         to = character(0),         nodes = names(data),         class = "PDAG"       )       as_disco(cg, kn)     }   ) }  register_engine("always_empty", always_empty_runner) empty_alg <- function(engine = "always_empty", ...) {   engine <- match.arg(engine)    make_method(     method_name = "empty_alg",     engine = engine,     engine_fns = list(       always_empty = function(...) {         make_runner(engine = "always_empty", alg = "empty_alg", ...)       }     ),     graph_class = "PDAG",     ...   ) } disco(tpc_example, empty_alg()) #> <Disco CPDAG: 6 nodes | 0 edges> #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 list_registered_engines() #> [1] "always_empty" reset_engine_registry()

title: Visualization
text: can visualize causal graphs using plot() function, works Knowledge Disco objects. function leverages underlying caugi::plot() method, providing flexible options customizing appearance nodes edges. use dataset num_data following examples, contains 5 numeric variables (X1, X2, X3, Y, Z). start creating simple Knowledge object visualizing plot().  default, required edges shown blue forbidden edges red. can customize colors using required_col forbidden_col arguments:  Different node layouts, node styles, edge styles can controlled via layout, node_style, edge_style parameters. illustrate simple example . full description available options, see documentation causalDisco::plot(), well underlying caugi::plot() function visualization vignette (vignette("visualization", "caugi")). use "fruchterman-reingold" layout customize node edge styles:  Note override colors required forbidden edges specific edge, edge needs targeted explicitly by_edge list edge_style argument. example, make required edge X1 X2 orange forbidden edge X2 Y yellow, letting edges use default colors, can :  can also pass custom layout plot():  can also visualize tiered knowledge structures. example using dataset variables measured different life stages:  Variables grouped life stage, reflecting tiered structure. helps visually convey temporal hierarchical relationships data. run causal discovery algorithm get Disco object, knowledge object alongside learned causal graph caugi::caugi object. can plot combined object see prior knowledge learned relationships  Blue edges indicate required relationships prior knowledge, black edges show learned data, forbidden edges plotted (avoid confusion clutter). tiered knowledge, plotting works similarly:  can see tiers reflected layout graph.
code: data(num_data) kn <- knowledge(   num_data,   X1 %-->% X2 + X3, # Require edge from X1 to X2, and X1 to X3   X2 %!-->% X3 + Y, # Forbid edge from X2 to X3, and X2 to Y   Y %!-->% Z # Forbid edge from Y to Z )  plot(kn) plot(kn, required_col = "skyblue", forbidden_col = "orange") plot(   kn,   layout = "fruchterman-reingold",   node_style = list(     fill = "lightblue", # Fill color     col = "darkblue", # Border color     lwd = 2, # Border width     padding = 4, # Text padding (mm)     size = 1.2 # Size multiplier   ),   edge_style = list(     lwd = 1.5, # Edge width     arrow_size = 4 # Arrow size (mm)   ),   required_col = "blue", # Color for required edges   forbidden_col = "red" # Color for forbidden edges ) plot(   kn,   layout = "fruchterman-reingold",   node_style = list(     fill = "lightblue", # Fill color     col = "darkblue", # Border color     lwd = 2, # Border width     padding = 4, # Text padding (mm)     size = 1.2 # Size multiplier   ),   edge_style = list(     lwd = 1.5, # Edge width     arrow_size = 4, # Arrow size (mm)     # Per-edge overrides     by_edge = list(       X1 = list(         X2 = list(col = "orange", fill = "orange", lwd = 3)       ),       X2 = list(         Y = list(col = "yellow", fill = "yellow", lwd = 3)       )     )   ),   required_col = "blue", # Color for required edges   forbidden_col = "red" # Color for forbidden edges ) my_layout <- data.frame(   name = c("X1", "X2", "X3", "Y", "Z"),   x = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5),   y = c(1, 2, 1, 2, 1) ) plot(kn, layout = my_layout) data(tpc_example) kn_tiered <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   tier(     child ~ starts_with("child"), # tidyselect helper; text: make_tikz() function exports plots clean, fully editable TikZ code inclusion LaTeX documents. Unlike graph export tools, edges attached nodes rather positioned using hard-coded coordinates, making output easier modify. functionality works Knowledge, Disco, caugi::caugi objects, allowing customize layouts, styles, edges LaTeX document. calls underlying causalDisco::plot() method (calls caugi::plot()) generate initial plot object converting TikZ code. Thus, can supply arguments make_tikz() supported causalDisco::plot() caugi::plot(). first demonstrate TikZ export Knowledge object. Setting full_doc = TRUE generates complete standalone LaTeX document can compiled directly. Using full_doc = FALSE instead returns tikzpicture environment, convenient inclusion inside existing LaTeX document. TikZ export also supports edge bending, can substantially improve readability edges pass nodes, can easily happen tiered knowledge structures. feature available standard caugi::plot() function. example, edge using standard straight style edge overlaps node youth_x3, bent edge avoids overlap:  TikZ plot can seen :  output disco() gives Disco object, can also exported TikZ: export mechanism also applies standard caugi::caugi objects:

title: R6 Interface to bnlearn Search Algorithms — BnlearnSearch
text: data data.frame holding data set currently attached search object. Can set set_data(). score Character scalar naming score function used bnlearn. Can set $set_score(). Kebab-case score names (used bnlearn, e.g. "pred-loglik") also accepted automatically translated snake_case. Recognised values : Continuous - Gaussian "aic_g", "bic_g", "ebic_g", "loglik_g", "pred_loglik_g" - gaussian versions respective scores discrete data. "bge" - Gaussian posterior density. "nal_g" - node-average log-likelihood. "pnal_g" - penalised node-average log-likelihood. Discrete – categorical "aic" - Akaike Information Criterion. "bdla" - locally averaged BDE. "bde" - Bayesian Dirichlet equivalent (uniform). "bds" - Bayesian Dirichlet score. "bic" - Bayesian Information Criterion. "ebic" - Extended BIC. "fnml" - factorised NML. "k2" - K2 score. "loglik" - log-likelihood. "mbde" - modified BDE. "nal" - node-average log-likelihood. "pnal" - penalised node-average log-likelihood. "pred_loglik" - predictive log-likelihood. "qnml" - quotient NML. Mixed Discrete/Gaussian "aic_cg", "bic_cg", "ebic_cg", "loglik_cg", "nal_cg", "pnal_cg", "pred_loglik_cg" - conditional Gaussian versions respective scores discrete data. test Character scalar naming conditional-independence test passed bnlearn. Can set $set_score(). Kebab-case test names (used bnlearn, e.g. "mi-adf") also accepted automatically translated snake_case. Recognised values : Continuous - Gaussian "cor" – Pearson correlation "fisher_z" / "zf" – Fisher Z test "mc_cor" – Monte Carlo Pearson correlation "mc_mi_g" – Monte Carlo mutual information (Gaussian) "mc_zf" – Monte Carlo Fisher Z "mi_g" – mutual information (Gaussian) "mi_g_sh" – mutual information (Gaussian, shrinkage) "smc_cor" – sequential Monte Carlo Pearson correlation "smc_mi_g" – sequential Monte Carlo mutual information (Gaussian) "smc_zf" – sequential Monte Carlo Fisher Z Discrete – categorical "mc_mi" – Monte Carlo mutual information "mc_x2" – Monte Carlo chi-squared "mi" – mutual information "mi_adf" – mutual information adjusted d.f. "mi_sh" – mutual information (shrinkage) "smc_mi" – sequential Monte Carlo mutual information "smc_x2" – sequential Monte Carlo chi-squared "sp_mi" – semi-parametric mutual information "sp_x2" – semi-parametric chi-squared "x2" – chi-squared "x2_adf" – chi-squared adjusted d.f. Discrete – ordered factors "jt" – Jonckheere–Terpstra "mc_jt" – Monte Carlo Jonckheere–Terpstra "smc_jt" – sequential Monte Carlo Jonckheere–Terpstra Mixed Discrete/Gaussian "mi_cg" / "conditional_gaussian" – mutual information (conditional Gaussian) Monte Carlo tests, set number permutations using B argument. alg Function generated $set_alg() runs structure-learning algorithm bnlearn. Period.case alg names (used bnlearn, e.g. "fast.iamb") also accepted automatically translated snake_case. Recognised values : Constraint-based "fast_iamb" – Fast-IAMB algorithm. See fast_iamb() underlying bnlearn::fast.iamb(). "gs" – Grow-Shrink algorithm. See gs() underlying bnlearn::gs(). "iamb" – Incremental Association Markov Blanket algorithm. See iamb() underlying bnlearn::iamb(). "iamb_fdr" – IAMB FDR control algorithm. See iamb_fdr() underlying bnlearn::iamb.fdr(). "inter_iamb" – Interleaved-IAMB algorithm. See inter_iamb() underlying bnlearn::inter.iamb(). "pc" – PC-stable algorithm. See pc() underlying bnlearn::pc.stable(). params list extra tuning parameters stored set_params() spliced learner call. knowledge list elements whitelist blacklist containing prior-knowledge constraints added via set_knowledge().

code: ### bnlearn_search R6 class examples ###  # Generally, we do not recommend using the R6 classes directly, but rather # use the disco() or any method function, for example pc(), instead.  # Load data data(num_data)  # Recommended: my_pc <- pc(engine = "bnlearn", test = "fisher_z", alpha = 0.05) result <- my_pc(num_data)  # or result <- disco(data = num_data, method = my_pc)  plot(result)   # Example with detailed settings: my_pc2 <- pc(   engine = "bnlearn",   test = "mi_g",   alpha = 0.01 ) disco(data = num_data, method = my_pc2) #> Warning: vstructure X1 -> Y <- X3 is not applicable, because one or both arcs are oriented in the opposite direction. #> Warning: vstructure X1 -> Y <- X2 is not applicable, because one or both arcs are oriented in the opposite direction. #> <Disco CPDAG: 5 nodes | 5 edges> #>   nodes: X1, X2, X3, Z, Y #>   edges: X2---X3, X2---Y, X3---Y, Y-->X1, Z-->X1  # With knowledge  kn <- knowledge(   num_data,   starts_with("X") %-->% Y )  disco(data = num_data, method = my_pc2, knowledge = kn) #> <Disco MPDAG: 5 nodes | 5 edges | Knowledge: 3 required> #> Learned graph: #>   nodes: X1, X2, X3, Z, Y #>   edges: X1-->Y, X1---Z, X2---X3, X2-->Y, X3-->Y #> Knowledge: #>   vars: X1, X2, X3, Y, Z #>   required: #>     X1-->Y #>     X2-->Y #>     X3-->Y  # Using additional test args (bootstrap samples)  my_iamb <- iamb(   engine = "bnlearn",   test = "mc_zf",   alpha = 0.05,   B = 100 )  disco(data = num_data, method = my_iamb) #> <Disco CPDAG: 5 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: X1, X2, X3, Z, Y #>   edges: X1-->Y, X1-->Z, X2---X3, X2-->Y, X3-->Y, Y-->Z  # Using R6 class: s <- BnlearnSearch$new()  s$set_data(num_data) s$set_test(method = "fisher_z", alpha = 0.05) s$set_alg("pc")  g <- s$run_search()  plot(g)

text: data data.frame holding data set currently attached search object. Can set set_data(). score function used build score, data set. Can set $set_score(). Recognized values : "tbic" - Temporal BIC score Gaussian data. See TemporalBIC. "tbdeu" - Temporal BDeu score discrete data. See TemporalBDeu. test function used test independence. Can set $set_test(). Recognized values : "fisher_z" - Fisher Z test Gaussian data. See cor_test(). "fisher_z_twd" - Fisher Z test Gaussian data test-wise deletion. See micd::gaussCItwd(). "fisher_z_mi" - Fisher Z test Gaussian data multiple imputation. See micd::gaussCItestMI(). "reg" - Regression test discrete binary data. See reg_test(). "g_square" - G square test discrete data. See pcalg::binCItest() pcalg::disCItest(). "g_square_twd" - G square test discrete data test-wise deletion. See micd::disCItwd(). "g_square_mi" - G square test discrete data multiple imputation. See micd::disMItest(). "conditional_gaussian" - Test conditional independence mixed data. See micd::mixCItest(). "conditional_gaussian_twd" - Test conditional independence mixed data test-wise deletion. See micd::mixCItwd(). "conditional_gaussian_mi" - Test conditional independence mixed data multiple imputation. See micd::mixMItest(). alg function used run search algorithm. Can set $set_alg(). Recognized values : "tfci" - TFCI algorithm. See tfci(). "tges" - TGES algorithm. See tges(). "tpc"  - TPC algorithm. See tpc(). Can also user-defined function; see $set_alg() details. params list parameters test algorithm. Can set $set_params(). TODO: secure yet terms distributing arguments. Use caution. suff_stat Sufficient statistic. format contents sufficient statistic depends test used. knowledge Knowledge object holding background knowledge.

code: # Generally, we do not recommend using the R6 classes directly, but rather # use the disco() or any method function, for example pc(), instead.  data(tpc_example)  # background knowledge (tiered knowledge) kn <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   tier(     child ~ starts_with("child"),     youth ~ starts_with("youth"),     old ~ starts_with("oldage")   ) )  # Recommended (TPC example): my_tpc <- tpc(engine = "causalDisco", test = "fisher_z", alpha = 0.05) result <- disco(data = tpc_example, method = my_tpc, knowledge = kn) plot(result)   # or my_tpc <- my_tpc |>   set_knowledge(kn) result <- my_tpc(tpc_example) plot(result)   # Using R6 class:  # --- Constraint-based: TPC ---------------------------------------------------- s_tpc <- CausalDiscoSearch$new() s_tpc$set_params(list(verbose = FALSE)) s_tpc$set_test("fisher_z", alpha = 0.2) s_tpc$set_alg("tpc") s_tpc$set_knowledge(kn) s_tpc$set_data(tpc_example) res_tpc <- s_tpc$run_search() print(res_tpc) #> <Disco UNKNOWN: 6 nodes | 6 edges | Knowledge: 3 tiers> #> Learned graph: #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x1---child_x2, child_x2-->oldage_x5, child_x2-->youth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3-->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6 #> Knowledge: #>   tier(child): child_x1, child_x2 #>   tier(youth): youth_x3, youth_x4 #>   tier(old): oldage_x5, oldage_x6  # Switch to TFCI on the same object (reuses suff_stat/test) s_tpc$set_alg("tfci") res_tfci <- s_tpc$run_search() print(res_tfci) #> <Disco UNKNOWN: 6 nodes | 6 edges | Knowledge: 3 tiers> #> Learned graph: #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x2o-ochild_x1, child_x2o->oldage_x5, child_x2o->youth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3o->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6 #> Knowledge: #>   tier(child): child_x1, child_x2 #>   tier(youth): youth_x3, youth_x4 #>   tier(old): oldage_x5, oldage_x6  # --- Score-based: TGES -------------------------------------------------------- s_tges <- CausalDiscoSearch$new() s_tges$set_score("tbic") # Gaussian temporal score s_tges$set_alg("tges") s_tges$set_data(tpc_example, set_suff_stat = FALSE) # suff stat not used for TGES s_tges$set_knowledge(kn) res_tges <- s_tges$run_search() print(res_tges) #> <Disco PDAG: 6 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x1---child_x2, child_x2-->oldage_x5, child_x2-->youth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3-->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6  # --- Custom (user-defined) algorithm: constraint-based ----------------------- my_alg <- function(data, knowledge, suff_stat) {   tpc_run(     data = data,     knowledge = knowledge,     suff_stat = suff_stat,     test = reg_test   ) }  s_custom <- CausalDiscoSearch$new() s_custom$set_test("reg") s_custom$set_knowledge(kn) s_custom$set_alg(my_alg) # type = "constraint" by default s_custom$set_data(tpc_example) res_custom <- s_custom$run_search() print(res_custom) #> <Disco UNKNOWN: 6 nodes | 6 edges | Knowledge: 3 tiers> #> Learned graph: #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x1---child_x2, child_x2-->oldage_x5, child_x2-->youth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3-->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6 #> Knowledge: #>   tier(child): child_x1, child_x2 #>   tier(youth): youth_x3, youth_x4 #>   tier(old): oldage_x5, oldage_x6  # --- Intentional error demonstrations ----------------------------------------  # run_search() without setting an algorithm try(CausalDiscoSearch$new()$run_search(tpc_example)) #> Error : Test must be set before sufficient statistic.  # set_suff_stat() requires data and test first s_err <- CausalDiscoSearch$new() try(s_err$set_suff_stat()) # no data & no test #> Error : Data must be set before sufficient statistic. s_err$set_data(tpc_example, set_suff_stat = FALSE) try(s_err$set_suff_stat()) # no test #> Error : Test must be set before sufficient statistic.  # unknown test / score / algorithm try(CausalDiscoSearch$new()$set_test("not_a_test")) #> Error : Unknown method: not_a_test try(CausalDiscoSearch$new()$set_score("not_a_score")) #> Error : Unknown score type using causalDisco engine: not_a_score try(CausalDiscoSearch$new()$set_alg("not_an_alg")) #> Error : Unknown method type using causalDisco engine: not_an_alg  # set_knowledge() requires a `Knowledge` object try(CausalDiscoSearch$new()$set_knowledge(list(not = "Knowledge"))) #> Error : Input must be a knowledge instance.

text: data data.frame holding data set currently attached search object. Can set set_data(). score function used build score, data set. Can set $set_score(). Recognized values : "sem_bic" - BIC score Gaussian observed data. See pcalg::GaussL0penObsScore. "sem_bic_int" - BIC score Gaussian data jointly interventional observational Gaussian data. See pcalg::GaussL0penIntScore. test function used test independence. Can set $set_test(). Recognized values : "fisher_z" - Fisher Z test Gaussian data. See pcalg::gaussCItest(). "fisher_z_twd" - Fisher Z test Gaussian data test-wise deletion. See micd::gaussCItwd(). "fisher_z_mi" - Fisher Z test Gaussian data multiple imputation. See micd::gaussCItestMI(). "reg" - Regression test discrete binary data. See reg_test(). "g_square" - G square test discrete data. See pcalg::binCItest() pcalg::disCItest(). "g_square_twd" - G square test discrete data test-wise deletion. See micd::disCItwd(). "g_square_mi" - G square test discrete data multiple imputation. See micd::disMItest(). "conditional_gaussian" - Test conditional independence mixed data. See micd::mixCItest(). "conditional_gaussian_twd" - Test conditional independence mixed data test-wise deletion. See micd::mixCItwd(). "conditional_gaussian_mi" - Test conditional independence mixed data multiple imputation. See micd::mixMItest(). alg function used run search algorithm. Can set $set_alg(). Recognized values : "fci" - FCI algorithm. See fci() underlying pcalg::fci(). "ges" - GES algorithm. See ges() underlying pcalg::ges(). "pc" - PC algorithm. See pc() underlying pcalg::pc(). "rfci" - RFCI algorithm. See rfci() underlying pcalg::rfci(). params list parameters test algorithm. Can set $set_params(). parameters passed test algorithm functions. suff_stat Sufficient statistic. format contents sufficient statistic depends test used. continuous Logical; whether sufficient statistic continuous test. continuous discrete TRUE, sufficient statistic build mixed test. discrete Logical; whether sufficient statistic discrete test. continuous discrete TRUE, sufficient statistic build mixed test. knowledge list fixed constraints search algorithm. Note, pcalg works symmetric knowledge. Thus, allowed types knowledge forbidden edges directions. adapt_df Logical; whether adapt degrees freedom discrete tests.

code: ### pcalg_search R6 class examples ###  # Generally, we do not recommend using the R6 classes directly, but rather # use the disco() or any method function, for example pc(), instead.  # Load data data(num_data)  # Recommended: my_pc <- pc(engine = "pcalg", test = "fisher_z") my_pc(num_data) #> <Disco PDAG: 5 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: X1, X2, X3, Z, Y #>   edges: X1-->Y, X1---Z, X2---X3, X2-->Y, X3-->Y, Z-->Y  # or disco(data = num_data, method = my_pc) #> <Disco CPDAG: 5 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: X1, X2, X3, Z, Y #>   edges: X1-->Y, X1---Z, X2---X3, X2-->Y, X3-->Y, Z-->Y  # Example with detailed settings: my_pc2 <- pc(   engine = "pcalg",   test = "fisher_z",   alpha = 0.01,   m.max = 4,   skel.method = "original" )  disco(data = num_data, method = my_pc2) #> The learned graph is not a valid CPDAG because of conflicting edge orientations, which can happen due to statistical errors in finite samples, violations of faithfulness, or latent confounding; it is reported as PDAG instead. #> <Disco PDAG: 5 nodes | 5 edges> #>   nodes: X1, X2, X3, Z, Y #>   edges: X1-->Y, X2---X3, X2-->Y, X3-->Y, Z-->X1  # With knowledge  kn <- knowledge(   num_data,   X1 %!-->% X2,   X2 %!-->% X1 )  disco(data = num_data, method = my_pc2, knowledge = kn) #> <Disco MPDAG: 5 nodes | 5 edges | Knowledge: 2 forbidden> #> Learned graph: #>   nodes: X1, X2, X3, Z, Y #>   edges: X1-->Y, X2---X3, X2-->Y, X3-->Y, Z-->X1 #> Knowledge: #>   vars: X1, X2, X3, Y, Z #>   forbidden: #>     X1!-->X2 #>     X2!-->X1  # Using R6 class: s <- PcalgSearch$new()  s$set_test(method = "fisher_z", alpha = 0.05) s$set_data(tpc_example) s$set_alg("pc")  g <- s$run_search()  print(g) #> <Disco PDAG: 6 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x2---child_x1, child_x2-->oldage_x5, child_x2---youth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3-->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6

title: Temporal Bayesian Dirichlet equivalent uniform (Score criterion) — TemporalBDeu-class
code: # For reproducibility set.seed(1405)  # Number of samples n <- 1000  # Define probabilities for A p_A <- c(0.4, 0.35, 0.25) # Probabilities for A = {1, 2, 3}  # Simulate A from a categorical distribution A <- sample(1:3, n, replace = TRUE, prob = p_A)  # Define conditional probabilities for B given A p_B_given_A <- list(   c(0.7, 0.3), # P(B | A=1)   c(0.4, 0.6), # P(B | A=2)   c(0.2, 0.8) # P(B | A=3) )  # Sample B based on A B <- sapply(A, function(a) sample(1:2, 1, prob = p_B_given_A[[a]]))  # Define conditional probabilities for C given A and B p_C_given_A_B <- list(   "1_1" = c(0.6, 0.4), # P(C | A=1, B=1)   "1_2" = c(0.3, 0.7), # P(C | A=1, B=2)   "2_1" = c(0.5, 0.5), # P(C | A=2, B=1)   "2_2" = c(0.2, 0.8), # P(C | A=2, B=2)   "3_1" = c(0.7, 0.3), # P(C | A=3, B=1)   "3_2" = c(0.4, 0.6) # P(C | A=3, B=2) )  # Sample C based on A and B C <- mapply(   function(a, b) sample(1:2, 1, prob = p_C_given_A_B[[paste(a, b, sep = "_")]]),   A,   B )  # Create dataset simdata <- data.frame(as.factor(A), as.factor(B), as.factor(C))  # Define order in prefix way colnames(simdata) <- c("child_A", "child_B", "adult_C") prefix_order <- c("child", "adult")  # Define Knowledge object kn <- knowledge(   simdata,   tier(     child ~ tidyselect::starts_with("child"),     adult ~ tidyselect::starts_with("adult")   ) )  # Define TemporalBDeu score t_score <- new("TemporalBDeu", knowledge = kn, data = simdata) # Run tges tges_pre <- tges_run(t_score)  # Plot MPDAG # plot(tges_pre)

title: R6 Interface to Tetrad Search Algorithms — TetradSearch
text: data Java object stores (possibly converted) data set used Tetrad. rdata Original R data.frame supplied user. score Java object holding scoring function selected set_score(). Supply one method strings set_score(). Recognised values : Continuous - Gaussian "ebic" - Extended BIC score. "gic" - Generalized Information Criterion (GIC) score. "poisson_prior" - Poisson prior score. "rank_bic" - Rank-based BIC score. "sem_bic" - SEM BIC score. "zhang_shen_bound" - Zhang Shen bound score. Discrete - categorical "bdeu" - Bayes Dirichlet Equivalent score uniform priors. "discrete_bic" - BIC score discrete data. Mixed Discrete/Gaussian "basis_function_bic" - BIC score basis-function models. generalization Degenerate Gaussian score. "basis_function_blocks_bic" - BIC score mixed data using basis-function models. "basis_function_sem_bic" - SEM BIC score basis-function models. "conditional_gaussian" - Conditional Gaussian BIC score. "degenerate_gaussian" - Degenerate Gaussian BIC score. "mag_degenerate_gaussian_bic" - MAG Degenerate Gaussian BIC Score. test Java object holding independence test selected set_test(). Supply one method strings set_test(). Recognised values : Continuous - Gaussian "fisher_z" - Fisher \(Z\) (partial correlation) test. "poisson_prior" - Poisson prior test. "rank_independence" - Rank-based independence test. "sem_bic" - SEM BIC test. Discrete - categorical "chi_square" - chi-squared test "g_square" - likelihood-ratio \(G^2\) test. "probabilistic" - Uses BCInference Cooper Bui calculate probabilistic conditional independence judgments. General "gin" - Generalized Independence Noise test. "kci" - Kernel Conditional Independence Test (KCI) Kun Zhang. "rcit" - Randomized Conditional Independence Test (RCIT). Mixed Discrete/Gaussian "basis_function_blocks" - Basis-function blocks test. "basis_function_lrt" - basis-function likelihood-ratio. "conditional_gaussian" - Conditional Gaussian test likelihood ratio test. "degenerate_gaussian" - Degenerate Gaussian test likelihood ratio test. alg Java object representing search algorithm. Supply one method strings set_alg(). Recognised values : Constraint-based "fci" - FCI algorithm. See fci(). "pc" - Peter-Clark (PC) algorithm. See pc(). "rfci" - Restricted FCI algorithm. See rfci(). Hybrid "boss_fci" - BOSS-FCI algorithm. See boss_fci(). "gfci" - GFCI algorithm. See gfci(). "grasp_fci" - GRaSP-FCI algorithm. See grasp_fci(). "sp_fci" - Sparsest Permutation using FCI. See sp_fci(). Score-based "boss" - BOSS algorithm. See boss(). "ges" ("fges") - (Fast) Greedy Equivalence Search (GES) algorithm. See ges(). "grasp" - GRaSP (Greedy Relations Sparsest Permutation) algorithm. See grasp(). mc_test Java independence-test object used Markov checker. java Java object returned search (typically graph). result Convenience alias java; may store additional metadata depending search type. knowledge Java Knowledge object carrying background constraints (required/forbidden edges). params Java Parameters object holding algorithm settings. bootstrap_graphs Java List graphs produced bootstrap resampling, feature requested. mc_ind_results Java List Markov-checker test results.

code: ### tetrad_search R6 class examples ###  # Generally, we do not recommend using the R6 classes directly, but rather # use the disco() or any method function, for example pc(), instead.  # Requires Tetrad to be installed if (verify_tetrad()$installed && verify_tetrad()$java_ok) {   data(num_data)    # Recommended:   my_pc <- pc(engine = "tetrad", test = "fisher_z")   my_pc(num_data)    # or   disco(data = num_data, method = my_pc)    # Example with detailed settings:   my_pc2 <- pc(     engine = "tetrad",     test = "sem_bic",     penalty_discount = 1,     structure_prior = 1,     singularity_lambda = 0.1   )   disco(data = num_data, method = my_pc2)    # Using R6 class:   s <- TetradSearch$new()    s$set_data(num_data)   s$set_test(method = "fisher_z", alpha = 0.05)   s$set_alg("pc")    g <- s$run_search()    print(g) } #> <Disco UNKNOWN: 5 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: X1, X2, X3, Z, Y #>   edges: X1-->Y, X1---Z, X2---X3, X2-->Y, X3-->Y, Z-->Y

code: data(tpc_example)  # create Knowledge object using verbs kn1 <- knowledge() |>   add_vars(names(tpc_example)) |>   add_tier(child) |>   add_tier(old, after = child) |>   add_tier(youth, before = old) |>   add_to_tier(child ~ starts_with("child")) |>   add_to_tier(youth ~ starts_with("youth")) |>   add_to_tier(old ~ starts_with("oldage")) |>   require_edge(child_x1 ~ youth_x3) |>   forbid_edge(child_x2 ~ youth_x4) |>   add_exogenous(child_x1) # synonym: add_exo()  # set kn1 to frozen # (meaning you cannot add variables to the Knowledge object anymore) # this is to get a true on the identical check kn1$frozen <- TRUE  # create identical Knowledge object using DSL kn2 <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   tier(     child ~ starts_with("child"),     youth ~ starts_with("youth"),     old ~ starts_with("oldage")   ),   child_x1 %-->% youth_x3,   child_x2 %!-->% youth_x4,   exo(child_x1) # synonym: exogenous() )  print(identical(kn1, kn2)) #> [1] TRUE  # cannot require an edge against tier direction try(   kn1 |> require_edge(oldage_x6 ~ child_x1) ) #> Error : Edge(s) violate tier ordering: oldage_x6 --> child_x1  # cannot forbid and require same edge try(   kn1 |> forbid_edge(child_x1 ~ youth_x3) ) #> Error : Edge(s) appear as both forbidden and required: child_x1 --> youth_x3

what: causalDisco: Causal Discovery in R — causalDisco-package
title: causalDisco: Causal Discovery in R — causalDisco-package
text: Tools causal structure learning observational data, emphasis temporally ordered variables. package implements Temporal Peter–Clark (TPC) algorithm (Petersen, Osler & Ekstrøm, 2021; doi:10.1093/aje/kwab087 ), Temporal Greedy Equivalence Search (TGES) algorithm (Larsen, Ekstrøm & Petersen, 2025; doi:10.48550/arXiv.2502.06232 ) Temporal Fast Causal Inference (TFCI). provides unified framework specifying background knowledge, can incorporated implemented algorithms R packages 'bnlearn' (Scutari, 2010; doi:10.18637/jss.v035.i03 ) 'pcalg' (Kalish et al., 2012; doi:10.18637/jss.v047.i11 ), well Java library 'Tetrad' (Scheines et al., 1998; doi:10.1207/s15327906mbr3301_3 ). package includes utilities visualization, comparison, evaluation graph structures, facilitating performance evaluation methodological studies.

title: Confusion Matrix — confusion
text: Adjacency comparison: confusion matrix cross-tabulation adjacencies. Hence, true positive means two inputs agree presence adjacency. true negative means two inputs agree adjacency. false positive means estimated graph places adjacency none. false negative means estimated graph place adjacency one. Orientation comparison: orientation confusion matrix conditional agreement adjacency. means adjacencies shared input matrices considered, agreement wrt. orientation computed among edges occur matrices. true positive correctly placed arrowhead (1), false positive marks placement arrowhead (1) tail (0), false negative marks placement tail (0) arrowhead (1), truth negative marks correct placement tail (0). supports caugi::caugi objects whose edges restricted -->, <->, ---, absence edge.

code: data(tpc_example)  # Recommended path using disco() fci_pcalg <- fci(engine = "pcalg", test = "fisher_z", alpha = 0.05) disco(tpc_example, fci_pcalg) #> <Disco PAG: 6 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x2o-ochild_x1, child_x2o->oldage_x5, child_x2o-oyouth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3o->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6  # or using fci_pcalg directly fci_pcalg(tpc_example) #> <Disco UNKNOWN: 6 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x2o-ochild_x1, child_x2o->oldage_x5, child_x2o-oyouth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3o->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6  # With all algorithm arguments specified fci_pcalg <- fci(   engine = "pcalg",   test = "fisher_z",   alpha = 0.05,   skel.method = "original",   type = "anytime",   fixedGaps = NULL,   fixedEdges = NULL,   NAdelete = FALSE,   m.max = 10,   pdsep.max = 2,   rules = c(rep(TRUE, 9), FALSE),   doPdsep = FALSE,   biCC = TRUE,   conservative = TRUE,   maj.rule = FALSE,   numCores = 1,   selectionBias = FALSE,   jci = "1",   verbose = FALSE ) disco(tpc_example, fci_pcalg) #> <Disco PAG: 6 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x2o-ochild_x1, child_x2o->oldage_x5, child_x2o-oyouth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3o->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6  #### Using tetrad engine with tier knowledge #### # Requires Tetrad to be installed if (verify_tetrad()$installed && verify_tetrad()$java_ok) {   kn <- knowledge(     tpc_example,     tier(       child ~ tidyselect::starts_with("child"),       youth ~ tidyselect::starts_with("youth"),       oldage ~ tidyselect::starts_with("oldage")     )   )    # Recommended path using disco()   fci_tetrad <- fci(engine = "tetrad", test = "fisher_z", alpha = 0.05)   disco(tpc_example, fci_tetrad, knowledge = kn)    # or using fci_tetrad directly   fci_tetrad <- fci_tetrad |> set_knowledge(kn)   fci_tetrad(tpc_example) } #> <Disco UNKNOWN: 6 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x2o-ochild_x1, child_x2o->oldage_x5, child_x2o-oyouth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3o->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6  # With all algorithm arguments specified if (verify_tetrad()$installed && verify_tetrad()$java_ok) {   fci_tetrad <- fci(     engine = "tetrad",     test = "fisher_z",     alpha = 0.05,     complete_rule_set_used = FALSE,     max_disc_path_length = 4,     depth = 10,     stable_fas = FALSE,     guarantee_pag = TRUE   )   disco(tpc_example, fci_tetrad) } #> <Disco PAG: 6 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x1o->child_x2, child_x2<->oldage_x5, child_x2<->youth_x4 #>          oldage_x6<->oldage_x5, youth_x3o->oldage_x5, youth_x4<->oldage_x6

code: data(tpc_example)  # create Knowledge object using verbs kn1 <- knowledge() |>   add_vars(names(tpc_example)) |>   add_tier(child) |>   add_tier(old, after = child) |>   add_tier(youth, before = old) |>   add_to_tier(child ~ starts_with("child")) |>   add_to_tier(youth ~ starts_with("youth")) |>   add_to_tier(old ~ starts_with("oldage")) |>   require_edge(child_x1 ~ youth_x3) |>   forbid_edge(child_x2 ~ youth_x4) |>   add_exogenous(child_x1) # synonym: add_exo()  # set kn1 to frozen # (meaning you cannot add variables to the Knowledge object anymore) # this is to get a true on the identical check kn1$frozen <- TRUE  # create identical Knowledge object using DSL kn2 <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   tier(     child ~ starts_with("child"),     youth ~ starts_with("youth"),     old ~ starts_with("oldage")   ),   child_x1 %-->% youth_x3,   child_x2 %!-->% youth_x4,   exo(child_x1) # synonym: exogenous() )  print(identical(kn1, kn2)) #> [1] TRUE  # cannot require an edge against tier direction try(   kn1 |> require_edge(oldage_x6 ~ child_x1) ) #> Error : Edge(s) violate tier ordering: oldage_x6 --> child_x1  # cannot forbid and require same edge try(   kn1 |> forbid_edge(child_x1 ~ youth_x3) ) #> Error : Edge(s) appear as both forbidden and required: child_x1 --> youth_x3

title: Define Background Knowledge — knowledge
text: ... Arguments define Knowledge object: Optionally, single data frame (first argument) whose column names initialize freeze variable set. Zero mini-DSL calls: tier(), exogenous(), (shorthand exo()), infix operators %-->%, %!-->%. tier(): One two-sided formulas (tier(1 ~ x + y)), numeric vector. exogenous() / exo(): Variable names tidyselect selectors. Arguments evaluated order; calls allowed.

title: Define Background Knowledge — knowledge

title: Define Background Knowledge — knowledge
text: Create Knowledge object using concise mini-DSL tier(), exogenous() infix edge operators %-->% %!-->%. first argument can data frame, used populate Knowledge object variable names. Supplying data frame also gives tidyselect helpers (e.g. tidyselect::starts_with()), set column names resolve , can used throughout mini-DSL, example tier(1 ~ starts_with("V")) everything() %-->% Y. later add variables add_* verbs, throw warning, since Knowledge object frozen. can unfreeze Knowledge object using function unfreeze(). data frame provided, object initially empty. Variables can added via tier(), forbidden(), required(), infix operators, add_vars(). tier(): Assigns variables tiers. Tiers may numeric string labels. left-hand side (LHS) formula tier; right-hand side (RHS) specifies variables. Variables can also selected using tidyselect syntax: tier(1 ~ starts_with("V")). %-->% %!-->%: Infix operators define required forbidden edges, respectively. sides operator can use tidyselect syntax select multiple variables. exogenous() / exo(): Mark variables exogenous. Numeric vector shortcut tier(): tier(c(1, 2, 1)) assigns tiers index existing variables. Multiple calls operators additive: call adds new edges Knowledge object. example:   results edges required - .e., union specified required edges.

title: Define Background Knowledge — knowledge
code: data(tpc_example)  # Knowledge objects can contain tier information, forbidden and required edges kn <- knowledge(   tier(     1 ~ V1 + V2,     2 ~ V3   ),   V1 %-->% V2,   V3 %!-->% V1 )  # If a data frame is provided, variable names are checked against it kn <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   tier(     1 ~ child_x1 + child_x2,     2 ~ youth_x3 + youth_x4,     3 ~ oldage_x5 + oldage_x6   ) )  # Throws error if variable not in data try(   knowledge(     tpc_example,     tier(       1 ~ child_x1 + child_x2,       2 ~ youth_x3 + youth_x4,       3 ~ oldage_x5 + woops     )   ) ) #> Error : Unknown variable(s): [woops] #> They are not present in the data frame provided to this Knowledge object.  # Using tidyselect helpers kn <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   tier(     1 ~ starts_with("child"),     2 ~ ends_with(c("_x3", "_x4")),     3 ~ starts_with("oldage")   ) )  # Numeric vector shortcut kn <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   tier(c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3)) )  # Custom tier naming kn <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   tier(     child ~ starts_with("child"),     youth ~ starts_with("youth"),     elderly ~ starts_with("oldage")   ) )  # There is also required and forbidden edges, which are specified like so kn <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   child_x1 %-->% youth_x3,   oldage_x6 %!-->% child_x1 )  # Both sides of an edge operator accept tidyselect helpers, so a set of edges # can be specified at once. Here every "child" variable is forbidden from # pointing to every "youth" variable. kn <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   starts_with("child") %!-->% starts_with("youth") )  # tidyselect set operations such as `!` (negation) and `&` (intersection) # also work. Forbid edges from child_x1 to every variable that is not a # "child" variable. kn <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   child_x1 %!-->% !starts_with("child") )  # You can also add exogenous variables kn <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   exogenous(child_x1),   exo(child_x2) # shorthand )  # Mix different operators kn <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   tier(     1 ~ starts_with("child") + youth_x4,     2 ~ youth_x3 + starts_with("oldage")   ),   child_x1 %-->% youth_x3,   oldage_x6 %!-->% oldage_x5,   exo(child_x2) )  # You can also build knowledge with a verb pipeline kn <-   knowledge() |>   add_vars(c("A", "B", "C", "D")) |> # Knowledge now only takes these variables   add_tier(One) |>   add_to_tier(One ~ A + B) |>   add_tier(2, after = One) |>   add_to_tier(2 ~ C + D) |>   forbid_edge(A ~ C) |>   require_edge(A ~ B)  # Mix DSL start + verb refinement kn <-   knowledge(     tier(1 ~ V5, 2 ~ V6),     V5 %!-->% V6   ) |>   add_tier(3, after = "2") |>   add_to_tier(3 ~ V7) |>   add_exo(V2) |>   add_exogenous(V3)  # Using seq_tiers for larger datasets large_data <- as.data.frame(   matrix(     runif(100),     nrow = 1,     ncol = 100,     byrow = TRUE   ) )  names(large_data) <- paste0("X_", 1:100)  kn <- knowledge(   large_data,   tier(     seq_tiers(       1:100,       ends_with("_{i}")     )   ),   X_1 %-->% X_2 )  small_data <- data.frame(   X_1 = 1,   X_2 = 2,   tier3_A = 3,   Y5_ok = 4,   check.names = FALSE )  kn <- knowledge(   small_data,   tier(     seq_tiers(1:2, ends_with("_{i}")),     seq_tiers(3, starts_with("tier{i}")),     seq_tiers(5, matches("Y{i}_ok"))   ) )

code: data(tpc_example)  #### Using pcalg engine #### # Recommended path using disco() pc_pcalg <- pc(engine = "pcalg", test = "fisher_z", alpha = 0.05) disco(tpc_example, pc_pcalg) #> <Disco CPDAG: 6 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x2---child_x1, child_x2-->oldage_x5, child_x2---youth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3-->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6  # or using pc_pcalg directly pc_pcalg(tpc_example) #> <Disco PDAG: 6 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x2---child_x1, child_x2-->oldage_x5, child_x2---youth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3-->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6  # With all algorithm arguments specified pc_pcalg <- pc(   engine = "pcalg",   test = "fisher_z",   alpha = 0.05,   fixedGaps = NULL,   fixedEdges = NULL,   NAdelete = FALSE,   m.max = 10,   u2pd = "relaxed",   skel.method = "original",   conservative = TRUE,   maj.rule = FALSE,   solve.confl = TRUE,   numCores = 1,   verbose = FALSE )  #### Using bnlearn engine with required knowledge #### kn <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   starts_with("child") %-->% starts_with("youth") )   # Recommended path using disco() pc_bnlearn <- pc(engine = "bnlearn", test = "fisher_z", alpha = 0.05) disco(tpc_example, pc_bnlearn, knowledge = kn) #> Warning: vstructure youth_x4 -> oldage_x6 <- oldage_x5 is not applicable, because one or both arcs are oriented in the opposite direction. #> <Disco MPDAG: 6 nodes | 9 edges | Knowledge: 4 required> #> Learned graph: #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x1---child_x2, child_x1-->youth_x3, child_x1-->youth_x4 #>          child_x2---oldage_x5, child_x2-->youth_x3, child_x2-->youth_x4 #>          oldage_x5---oldage_x6, oldage_x5-->youth_x3, oldage_x6-->youth_x4 #> Knowledge: #>   vars: child_x1, child_x2, oldage_x5, oldage_x6, youth_x3, youth_x4 #>   required: #>     child_x1-->youth_x3 + youth_x4 #>     child_x2-->youth_x3 + youth_x4  # or using pc_bnlearn directly pc_bnlearn <- pc_bnlearn |> set_knowledge(kn) pc_bnlearn(tpc_example) #> Warning: vstructure youth_x4 -> oldage_x6 <- oldage_x5 is not applicable, because one or both arcs are oriented in the opposite direction. #> <Disco PDAG: 6 nodes | 9 edges> #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x1---child_x2, child_x1-->youth_x3, child_x1-->youth_x4 #>          child_x2---oldage_x5, child_x2-->youth_x3, child_x2-->youth_x4 #>          oldage_x5---oldage_x6, oldage_x5-->youth_x3, oldage_x6-->youth_x4   # With all algorithm arguments specified pc_bnlearn <- pc(   engine = "bnlearn",   test = "fisher_z",   alpha = 0.05,   max.sx = 2,   debug = FALSE,   undirected = TRUE )  disco(tpc_example, pc_bnlearn) #> The learned graph is not a valid CPDAG because of conflicting edge orientations, which can happen due to statistical errors in finite samples, violations of faithfulness, or latent confounding; it is reported as PDAG instead. #> <Disco PDAG: 6 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x1---child_x2, child_x2---oldage_x5, child_x2---youth_x4 #>          oldage_x5---oldage_x6, oldage_x5---youth_x3, oldage_x6---youth_x4  #### Using tetrad engine with tier knowledge #### # Requires Tetrad to be installed if (verify_tetrad()$installed && verify_tetrad()$java_ok) {   kn <- knowledge(     tpc_example,     tier(       child ~ tidyselect::starts_with("child"),       youth ~ tidyselect::starts_with("youth"),       oldage ~ tidyselect::starts_with("oldage")     )   )    # Recommended path using disco()   pc_tetrad <- pc(engine = "tetrad", test = "fisher_z", alpha = 0.05)   disco(tpc_example, pc_tetrad, knowledge = kn)    # or using pc_tetrad directly   pc_tetrad <- pc_tetrad |> set_knowledge(kn)   pc_tetrad(tpc_example) } #> <Disco UNKNOWN: 6 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x2---child_x1, child_x2-->oldage_x5, child_x2-->youth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3-->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6  # With all algorithm arguments specified if (verify_tetrad()$installed && verify_tetrad()$java_ok) {   pc_tetrad <- pc(     engine = "tetrad",     test = "fisher_z",     alpha = 0.05,     conflict_rule = 2,     depth = 10,     stable_fas = FALSE,     guarantee_cpdag = TRUE   )   disco(tpc_example, pc_tetrad) } #> <Disco CPDAG: 6 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x2---child_x1, child_x2-->oldage_x5, child_x2---youth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3-->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6

title: Plot a Disco Object — plot.Disco
code: data(tpc_example)  # Define tiered knowledge kn <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   tier(     child ~ starts_with("child"),     youth ~ starts_with("youth"),     old ~ starts_with("old")   ) )  # Fit a causal discovery model cd_tges <- tges(engine = "causalDisco", score = "tbic") disco_cd_tges <- disco(data = tpc_example, method = cd_tges, knowledge = kn)  # Plot with default column orientation plot(disco_cd_tges)   # Plot with row orientation plot(disco_cd_tges, orientation = "rows")   # Plot with custom node and edge styling plot(   disco_cd_tges,   node_style = list(     fill = "lightblue", # Fill color     col = "darkblue", # Border color     lwd = 2, # Border width     padding = 4, # Text padding (mm)     size = 1.2 # Size multiplier   ),   edge_style = list(     lwd = 1.5, # Edge width     arrow_size = 4, # Arrow size (mm)     col = "darkgreen", # Edge color     fill = "black", # Arrow fill color     lty = "dashed" # Edge line type   ) )   # To override a specific edge style which is required you need to target that individual node: kn <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   tier(     child ~ starts_with("child"),     youth ~ starts_with("youth"),     old ~ starts_with("old")   ),   child_x1 %-->% child_x2 + youth_x4 # required edges ) bnlearn_pc <- pc(engine = "bnlearn", test = "fisher_z") disco_bnlearn_pc <- disco(data = tpc_example, method = bnlearn_pc, knowledge = kn)  # Edge from child_x1 to child_x2 will be orange, but edge from child_x1 to youth_x4 # will be required_col (blue) since we only override the child_x1 to child_x2 edge. plot(   disco_bnlearn_pc,   edge_style = list(     by_edge = list(       child_x1 = list(         child_x2 = list(col = "orange", fill = "orange")       )     )   ),   required_col = "blue" )   # Plot without tiers data(num_data) kn_untiered <- knowledge(   num_data,   X1 %-->% X2 + X3,   Z %!-->% Y )  bnlearn_pc <- pc(engine = "bnlearn", test = "fisher_z") res_untiered <- disco(data = num_data, method = bnlearn_pc, knowledge = kn_untiered) #> The learned graph is not a valid MPDAG because the background knowledge conflicts with the structure learned from the data; it is reported as PDAG instead. plot(res_untiered)   # With a custom defined layout custom_layout <- data.frame(  name = c("X1", "X2", "X3", "Z", "Y"),  x = c(0, 1, 2, 2, 3),  y = c(0, 1, 0.25, -1, 0) ) plot(res_untiered, layout = custom_layout)

code: data(tpc_example)  # Define a `Knowledge` object with tiers kn_tiered <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   tier(     child ~ starts_with("child"),     youth ~ starts_with("youth"),     old ~ starts_with("old")   ) )  # Simple plot (default column orientation) plot(kn_tiered)   # Plot with row orientation plot(kn_tiered, orientation = "rows")   # Plot with custom node styling, edge width/arrow size and edge colors kn <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   tier(     child ~ starts_with("child"),     youth ~ starts_with("youth"),     old ~ starts_with("old")   ),   child_x1 %-->% child_x2, # required edge   youth_x4 %!-->% youth_x3  # forbidden edge ) plot(   kn,   node_style = list(     fill = "lightblue", # Fill color     col = "darkblue", # Border color     lwd = 2, # Border width     padding = 4, # Text padding (mm)     size = 1.2 # Size multiplier   ),   edge_style = list(     lwd = 1.5, # Edge width     arrow_size = 4 # Arrow size (mm)   ),   required_col = "darkgreen",   forbidden_col = "darkorange" )   # To override a specific edge style which is required/forbidden # you need to target that individual node: kn <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   tier(     child ~ starts_with("child"),     youth ~ starts_with("youth"),     old ~ starts_with("old")   ),   child_x1 %-->% child_x2 + youth_x4, # required edges   youth_x4 %!-->% youth_x3 + oldage_x5  # forbidden edges )  # Edge from child_x1 to child_x2 will be orange, but edge from child_x1 to youth_x4 # will be required_col (blue) since we only override the child_x1 to child_x2 edge. # Similarly, edge from youth_x4 to youth_x3 will be yellow, but edge from youth_x4 # to oldage_x5 will be forbidden_col (red). plot(   kn,   edge_style = list(     by_edge = list(       child_x1 = list(         child_x2 = list(col = "orange", fill = "orange")       ),       youth_x4 = list(         youth_x3 = list(col = "yellow", fill = "yellow")       )     )   ),   required_col = "blue",   forbidden_col = "red" )   # Define a `Knowledge` object without tiers kn_untiered <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   child_x1 %-->% child_x2 + youth_x3,   youth_x4 %!-->% oldage_x5 ) # Plot with default layout plot(kn_untiered)   # With a custom defined layout custom_layout <- data.frame(  name = c("child_x1", "child_x2", "youth_x3", "youth_x4", "oldage_x5", "oldage_x6"),  x = c(0, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4),  y = c(0, 1, 0, -1, 0, 1) ) plot(kn_untiered, layout = custom_layout)

code: data(tpc_example)  # create Knowledge object using verbs kn1 <- knowledge() |>   add_vars(names(tpc_example)) |>   add_tier(child) |>   add_tier(old, after = child) |>   add_tier(youth, before = old) |>   add_to_tier(child ~ starts_with("child")) |>   add_to_tier(youth ~ starts_with("youth")) |>   add_to_tier(old ~ starts_with("oldage")) |>   require_edge(child_x1 ~ youth_x3) |>   forbid_edge(child_x2 ~ youth_x4) |>   add_exogenous(child_x1) # synonym: add_exo()  # set kn1 to frozen # (meaning you cannot add variables to the Knowledge object anymore) # this is to get a true on the identical check kn1$frozen <- TRUE  # create identical Knowledge object using DSL kn2 <- knowledge(   tpc_example,   tier(     child ~ starts_with("child"),     youth ~ starts_with("youth"),     old ~ starts_with("oldage")   ),   child_x1 %-->% youth_x3,   child_x2 %!-->% youth_x4,   exo(child_x1) # synonym: exogenous() )  print(identical(kn1, kn2)) #> [1] TRUE  # cannot require an edge against tier direction try(   kn1 |> require_edge(oldage_x6 ~ child_x1) ) #> Error : Edge(s) violate tier ordering: oldage_x6 --> child_x1  # cannot forbid and require same edge try(   kn1 |> forbid_edge(child_x1 ~ youth_x3) ) #> Error : Edge(s) appear as both forbidden and required: child_x1 --> youth_x3

code: data(tpc_example)  # Recommended path using disco() rfci_pcalg <- rfci(engine = "pcalg", test = "fisher_z", alpha = 0.05) disco(tpc_example, rfci_pcalg) #> <Disco RFCI-PAG: 6 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x2o-ochild_x1, child_x2o->oldage_x5, child_x2o-oyouth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3o->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6  # or using rfci_pcalg directly rfci_pcalg(tpc_example) #> <Disco UNKNOWN: 6 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x2o-ochild_x1, child_x2o->oldage_x5, child_x2o-oyouth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3o->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6  # With all algorithm arguments specified rfci_pcalg <- rfci(   engine = "pcalg",   test = "fisher_z",   alpha = 0.05,   skel.method = "original",   fixedGaps = NULL,   fixedEdges = NULL,   NAdelete = FALSE,   m.max = 10,   rules = c(rep(TRUE, 9), FALSE),   conservative = TRUE,   maj.rule = FALSE,   numCores = 1,   verbose = FALSE ) disco(tpc_example, rfci_pcalg) #> <Disco RFCI-PAG: 6 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x2o-ochild_x1, child_x2o->oldage_x5, child_x2o-oyouth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3o->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6  #### Using tetrad engine with tier knowledge #### # Requires Tetrad to be installed if (verify_tetrad()$installed && verify_tetrad()$java_ok) {   kn <- knowledge(     tpc_example,     tier(       child ~ tidyselect::starts_with("child"),       youth ~ tidyselect::starts_with("youth"),       oldage ~ tidyselect::starts_with("oldage")     )   )    # Recommended path using disco()   rfci_tetrad <- rfci(engine = "tetrad", test = "fisher_z", alpha = 0.05)   disco(tpc_example, rfci_tetrad, knowledge = kn)    # or using rfci_tetrad directly   rfci_tetrad <- rfci_tetrad |> set_knowledge(kn)   rfci_tetrad(tpc_example) } #> <Disco UNKNOWN: 6 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x2o-ochild_x1, child_x2o->oldage_x5, child_x2o-oyouth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3o->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6  # With all algorithm arguments specified if (verify_tetrad()$installed && verify_tetrad()$java_ok) {   rfci_tetrad <- rfci(     engine = "tetrad",     test = "fisher_z",     alpha = 0.05,     depth = 10,     stable_fas = FALSE,     max_disc_path_length = 2,     complete_rule_set_used = TRUE   )   disco(tpc_example, rfci_tetrad) } #> <Disco RFCI-PAG: 6 nodes | 6 edges> #>   nodes: child_x2, child_x1, youth_x4, youth_x3, oldage_x6, oldage_x5 #>   edges: child_x2o-ochild_x1, child_x2o->oldage_x5, child_x2o-oyouth_x4 #>          oldage_x5-->oldage_x6, youth_x3o->oldage_x5, youth_x4-->oldage_x6
